note: Sepolia receipts for ETHGlobal Tokyo 2026. Every field was fetched from the chain, not typed. CLAUDE.md: an unchecked receipt is worth less than no receipt, because it looks like evidence.

agentOwner.role: owns agentId 10518; its own write is refused

secondAddress.role: not owner, not an approved operator; its write is accepted
secondAddress.constraint: MUST NOT be approved on the agent token. isAuthorizedOrOwner is ERC-721's standard check, so one approve() would make this address refused too and the second shot would stop existing.

buyer.role: the client. A third account on purpose: reusing the second address from beat 1 would have made the demo's happy path the self-dealing case the project says it cannot prevent.

erc8004.provenance: erc-8004/erc-8004-contracts, deployed by the 8004 team, used unmodified
erc8004.andTheSpec: erc-8004.md:217 requires it. The ChaosChain reference implementation does NOT enforce it; we use the official contracts and show their check working first.

register.note: reckn-arc registers the agent. agentId 10518, minted to the EOA that is refused below.

selfWriteRefused.note: the agent's OWN address calls giveFeedback for its own agentId. Mined and reverted: Self-feedback not allowed. Sent with an explicit gas limit so estimation could not swallow it -- a refusal nobody can click is weaker than one they can.

secondAddressAccepted.note: a second address the same operator controls makes the identical call, and it succeeds. The check asks who you are; a second address answers it.

deployEscrow.note: RecknZkEscrow on Sepolia. No constructor, so the deployment carries no parameters. ENS Continuity asks the integration to target an existing project's testnet deployment; before tonight the escrow was on Arc only.

deployVerdictVerifier.note: RecknVerdictVerifier, pointing at SP1 v6.1.0 Groth16 0xb69f2584, which has NO owner. Not the SP1VerifierGateway: the gateway has an owner and its route for our selector is unfrozen, and a project whose claim is that no key decides should not put an owner in the adjudication path.

deployParentRegistry.note: our PermissionedRegistry, with ENS's own LabelStore 0x375c0820 (reached by ETHRegistrar -> ETH_REGISTRY -> LABEL_STORE, not guessed). Root roles held by the deployer FOR NOW; they are renounced after the adapter is granted.

deployResolverProxy.note: a UUPS proxy of ENS's PermissionedResolver implementation, created through ENS's own VerifiableFactory rather than a proxy of ours. The implementation is UUPS, so an EIP-1167 clone dies inside onlyProxy with 210 gas and no revert data.

approveRegistrar.note: MockUSDC allowance for the ETHRegistrar; ENSv2 registration fees are paid in MockUSDC on Sepolia.

commitName.note: commit-then-register: the commitment for reckn. MIN_COMMITMENT_AGE is 60 seconds, read from the registrar.

registerName.note: reckn registered on the REAL Sepolia ETHRegistrar for 0.613701 MockUSDC, with our PermissionedRegistry as its subregistry and our proxy as its resolver.

issueAgentSubname.note: agent.reckn.eth issued to the agent with roleBitmap 65536 = ROLE_RENEW ONLY. No ROLE_SET_RESOLVER: the agent owns its name and is not given the power to repoint its own record surface.

deployAdapter.note: SettlementRecord. No owner, no admin, no pause, no upgrade; open() and close() are callable by anyone and neither can choose an outcome.

grantAdapterOnResolver.note: the adapter is given the resolver role it needs to open and close windows.

revokeGhostGrant.note: an earlier grant went to 0xF3Ef66B7, the address the adapter was PREDICTED to land on before two funding transactions moved the nonce. Nothing is there and nothing can ever be: that CREATE address needs reckn-arc nonce 13, which was spent on a transfer. Revoked anyway -- 013 R-6 asks whether a second admin can appear later, and an unexplained root grant in the state is not an answer.

mintBuyerUsdc.note: MockUSDC for the buyer; its mint has no owner guard.

joinFund.note: the buyer funds 250 USDC and names the verifier, pinned by codehash.

joinSettle.note: somebody who is NOT the buyer settles it on a real Groth16 proof. settleWithProof is permissionless.

joinOpen.note: the adapter opens the one window this deal will ever have, for the buyer fixed at funding. The caller chose nothing.

joinWrite.note: the BUYER writes the record. The agent never held this right.

joinClose.note: the window closes. The buyer's second write now reverts too.

deployRehearsal.note: throwaway CREATE, pre-event, to prove the keystore/RPC/gas/explorer path before the window. WARNING: its address equals arc.json's RecknVerdictVerifier, because both are reckn-arc nonce 1 on their own chain. It is NOT a verifier.

fundSecondAddress.note: 0.005 ETH to the second address. Pre-event infrastructure.

stateReadBack.why: the owner wrote nothing and a second address wrote one record. This is state, not transactions, and it is what beat 1 claims.
routes to 0x740e02ce…, our resolver — E-Q3 satisfied on the real resolution path
stateReadBack.setResolver by the agent itself: STILL SUCCEEDS, because the deployer holds ROOT roles on the parent registry. S4's claim closes only after those are renounced, which happens after the adapter is granted. 013 section 1.1 discloses exactly this residue; it is not yet closed and is not claimed to be.

deployed.note: bytecode of the two Reckn contracts was compared against `forge inspect`, not against out/ (a stale artifact there produced a false mismatch once tonight). The verifier differs from its artifact only where its two immutables are substituted, and those hold the intended values.

ens.family: the deployment family the spikes measured against; three live ENSv2 families exist on Sepolia and mixing them silently produces a name nobody can resolve
ens.name: reckn.eth

afterwards.THE AGENT writes: STILL SUCCEEDS. reckn-arc is both the agent and the account still holding root on the resolver and the registry. 013 section 1.1 discloses this residue; renouncing is what closes it, and it has not been done because redeploying the adapter would then be impossible. It MUST be done before filming, or beat 2's refusal is not true on chain.
